reviewed_hunks.quote: Technology-based prompts raise engagement versus nothing (RR 1.27, 14 trials, PMID 26747176), best when they announce new content early — but the effect is borderline and heterogeneous, and unsolicited push would trade against the autonomy the whole design protects. So the in-app notices are the whole prompt layer: milestones, far-check due cards, weekly-goal nudges. No push channel, no inbox, no badge. A companion review of mHealth adherence drivers (99 studies, PMID 35612886) adds personalization, reminders and usable stable design on the plus side — and names technical difficulties the top barrier, which makes stability itself an adherence intervention. See R22, R53.
